{{Short description|Theorem in Boolean algebra}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=May 2023|cs1-dates=y}}
{{Use list-defined references|date=May 2023}}
In [[Boolean algebra]], '''Poretsky's law of forms''' shows that the single Boolean equation <math>f(X)=0</math> is equivalent to <math>g(X)=h(X)</math> if and only if <math>g=f\oplus h</math>, where <math>\oplus</math> represents [[exclusive or]].

The law of forms was discovered by [[Platon Poretsky]].
